query: Other People's Candles {Halfway up the seventh tower is a landing crowded with candle stubs, a century of them, with initials scratched in the wall above. Whoever climbed here, climbed with a light.|The candle landing. You recognise some of the initials now, the way you recognise faces in a corridor.|Back at the landing of candles. You've found your own favourite set of initials, deep and careful, and wonder who cut them.} {One stub is still faintly warm.|{season == "winter": The wax is cold as stone.|A draught from nowhere leans every wick the same way.}|One stub has been lit and blown out since your last climb.} Leave a candle of your own {You light the candle you bought in the village and set it among the others. For a moment the landing is bright, and the initials look almost cheerful.|You light a new candle and sit with it while it burns down. It feels like adding your name to a very long, very quiet register.|You leave a fresh candle beside the careful initials. When you look back from the stair, its flame is leaning toward them.} Read the initials by lamplight {You copy down the initials and the dates. Most of them are a century old or more; one is from last year. Nobody you ask admits to it.|You find two sets of initials cut in the same hand, forty years apart. You leave without deciding what that means.|You read the wall until your lamp gutters. All those people, climbing up here with a light, alone. It sits with you all evening.}
